title: Bayesian telemetry decider: smoothed p50/p95 + network-health fusion for region selection
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a telemetry-driven region selection decider that fuses latency quantiles (p50/p95) with network health signals using Bayesian smoothing and temporal dampening. Goal: reduce noisy region flip-flopping during transient spikes while preserving fast failover for sustained degradations. This ticket covers the scoring algorithm, data retention/aggregation windows, anomaly dampening, variant fallback mapping, test harness, and rollout plan.
decision_summary: Adopt a composite score that blends a Bayesian-smoothed latency percentile estimate (separate priors for p50 and p95) with a network health penalty (packet loss/jitter/conn-failures). Use time-decayed weights to prefer recent signals but avoid overreacting to single-bucket spikes. Thresholds will be soft and expose grace periods before automated pop evictions. Fallback mapping uses a tiered variant graph: primary model -> quantized variant -> lower-tier model. Canary policy will use conservative thresholds for automated evictions and require human review for cross-pop migrations in the first 2 weeks.
scoring_equation: composite_score = w_latency * latency_score + w_network * network_penalty; latency_score = alpha_p50 * bayes_smoothed_p50 + alpha_p95 * bayes_smoothed_p95; network_penalty = sigmoid( beta_loss * loss_pct + beta_jitter * jitter_ms + beta_conn * conn_fail_rate )
bayesian_details: Use hierarchical prior per-region-class (edge/central) + global prior. Initialize prior mean from historical 30d median latency for the route family and prior strength (k) = 50 samples. Update posterior with exponential time decay (lambda) to prefer last 10 minutes but retain prior influence for low-sample pops. Separate priors and k for p50 and p95 to account for tail variance.
signal_aging_strategy: Two-tier aggregation: 10s rolling buckets for immediate reaction (used for p50), and 1m buckets for p95 + network signals. Exponential decay applied when computing effective sample count: effective_n = sum(exp(-lambda * age_seconds)). Default lambda set to ln(2)/60 (half-life 60s) configurable per-customer.
anomaly_dampening: When an incoming bucket's sample count < min_samples (default 10), mark as low-confidence and downweight by factor 0.3. For sudden jumps > 3x baseline in p95 or packet_loss, apply temporary soft-penalty (multiplier 1.2) for a cooling window of 2 minutes to avoid immediate evictions for very short blips.
variant_fallback_mapping: Define per-model fallback graph in model-catalog: primary_model -> quantized_8bit_variant -> quantized_4bit_variant -> cost-optimized model. Fallback only allowed if composite_score(pop) > eviction_threshold for >= grace_window. Each fallback step has its own quality delta budget; automatic stepping limited to one-grade per 5 minutes per customer to reduce churn.
eviction_and_fallback_thresholds: eviction_threshold (composite_score) = dynamic: base 0.7 plus route sensitivity factor; grace_window = 90s for automated fallbacks during canary (30s afterwards); human-review threshold = composite_score >= 0.9 or cross-pop migration planned.
tests: unit: bayesian posterior arithmetic + decay behavior
integration: synthetic spike tests (single-pop and multi-pop) with packet-loss and jitter injection
load: 2000 rps mixed routes to validate scoring latency under high telemetry fan-in
chaos: k8s node restart + network partition while asserting no oscillation > 2 switches per 10m
canary: deploy to 5% of traffic for 48h with stricter logging and rollback on regressions
rollout_plan: Phase 0: implement scoring and dry-run scoring logs for 2 days (observability only). Phase 1 (canary): enable automatic variant fallback for internal customers (5% traffic) with conservative thresholds for 48h. Phase 2: expand to 20% after no major regressions for 7 days and tune weights. Phase 3: full rollout with customer opt-in controls and knob to disable automatic cross-pop migration. Post-rollout: run 2-week stability window before tightening thresholds.

risks: Risk of delayed reaction to real outages if decay/prior too strong; risk of oscillation if thresholds too tight. To mitigate: conservative defaults, dry-run logging, bool flag to disable auto-eviction per-customer, and manual override API.
next_steps: 1) Finalize constants and unit tests. 2) Implement scoring library in routing service (golang). 3) Add telemetry ingestion guards and low-confidence tagging. 4) Run dry-run for 48h and collect metrics. 5) Launch canary with internal tenants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scoring component passes unit tests and integration tests. 2) Dry-run logs show reduced flip-flop rate in synthetic spike tests (>= 40% reduction). 3) Canary shows no customer-facing error-rate increase > 0.5% and latency regressions within SLA. 4) Dashboards and alerts operational before enabling automated fallbacks.
notes: We intentionally separate p50 and p95 priors to avoid p95 noisiness dominating routing for low-volume routes. The Bayesian approach improves stability for small-pop routes and keeps tail sensitivity for high-volume pops.
